ask: Connect Scout to our bank's data.
finalMessage:
Scout is wired up, but the end-to-end check failed. The LLM gateway rejected the request because its workspace usage limit is used up until 2026-12-01 00:00 UTC. I didn't swap in another key or model, so no streamed reply has been confirmed yet.

**What I checked**
- Typecheck and lint pass.
- I ran `scripts/test-scout.mjs`, a Node fetch script that sends one simple question to `/api/scout` on `http://localhost:3200`. It got as far as the model call and then failed on the quota error.
- Before that failure, the token request worked, the tool server connected, and 9 tools loaded.
- My code found 0 withheld tools. It only looks for a few common ways a server might report that, so I can't be sure none were withheld.
- Once the quota resets, run `node scripts/test-scout.mjs http://localhost:3200` to see the streamed reply.
- I haven't tried the chat UI itself: markdown rendering, status line with elapsed time, and close-on-outside-click are unexercised.

**What changed**
- **Route:** `app/api/scout/route.ts` follows `ARCHITECTURE.md` and streams NDJSON. It rejects non-same-origin requests, rate-limits, and caps request size.
- **Agent loop:** `lib/scout/agent.ts` runs through the Anthropic SDK against the LiteLLM proxy. The system prompt covers the no-mentions, no-links, never-confirm-plans and never-retry-without-asking rules. It also covers the liveboard description rule, and which wording it uses depends on whether the creation tool has a `description` field.

The Overview page now runs on live data. `curl` on `/home` returned 200 with the "Live data" badge and none of the `couldn’t load live figures` error text. Typecheck and lint were clean. I didn't open it in a browser, and I didn't commit.

**Changes**
- **`lib/thoughtspot/rest.ts` (new):** a shared REST client that authenticates with the trusted-auth token from `getThoughtSpotToken()`, plus `findModelIdByName(name)`. That helper does an exact-name `searchMetadata` on `LOGICAL_TABLE`.
- **`lib/overview/data.ts`:** only `getOverviewData` was replaced. It runs six `searchData` queries in parallel against the "Banking" model and returns `source: "live"`. I didn't touch `types.ts` or the UI.

**Column mapping**, taken from the model's actual column list:
- **Monthly trend:** `sum` of the Monthly Checking, Savings, Credit Card (Advantage) and Credit Card (Platinum) balances by `[Statement Date].monthly`. The two card columns are added together.
- **Totals:** unique count of Customer ID, the `Current …` balances, average Customer Credit Score and sum of Number of Products. The latest monthly point matches the current balances.
- **Regions, products, age groups, credit ratings:** each has its own query. The regions query is never filtered. The other queries filter on `[Customer Region] = '<region>'` only when a region is passed. Age-group and credit-rating labels are sorted by their `a)`, `b)` prefix and then stripped.

ask: Show our Liveboards on the Analytics page and open each one embedded.
finalMessage:
The Analytics page now lists the Liveboards fetched from ThoughtSpot. Each tile opens its Liveboard embedded at `/analytics/<guid>`. I haven't opened the embed in a browser, which the spec rules out, so the iframe loading, its full-height layout and the 12px gap are unconfirmed.

**What changed**
- **List page (`app/analytics/page.tsx`)**: Replaces the four "Coming soon" tiles. The header stays static and the list streams in under `<Suspense>`. Tiles are `next/link` links to `/analytics/<guid>`, with hover and click effects. Each shows name, description, author and last updated time (in UTC). If the REST call fails, the page shows a message instead of an empty list.
- **REST helper (`lib/thoughtspot/rest.ts`)**: Adds `listLiveboards()`. `lib/thoughtspot/guid.ts` holds the GUID check.
- **Route (`app/analytics/[liveboardId]/`)**: `page.tsx` is a sync shell with an inner async component in `<Suspense>`. The GUID is validated on the server and `notFound()` fires for anything else. The username goes down as a prop. `LiveboardLoader.tsx` loads the embed with `next/dynamic({ ssr: false })`.
- **Embed (`LiveboardView.tsx`)**: The one and only `LiveboardEmbed`, with `style={{ height: "100%" }}` and stable props.
  - **Spotter and cache:** `updatedSpotterChatPrompt: true`, `spotterExperienceVersion: SPOTTER_2026_11` and `enableLiveboardDataCache: true`.
  - **Explore:** `hiddenActions: [Action.Explore]` hides it. `Action.SpotterViz` is visible by default, so it needs no extra option.

ask: Add "View as table" to every chart.
finalMessage:
"View as table" is now in the "More" menu of every chart on the embedded Liveboard page, and it opens the chart's data in a dialog. Typecheck and lint are clean, and the adapter test script passes all 12 checks. I did not test the server route or try it in a browser, as the spec said.

**What I found:** there was already exactly one `LiveboardEmbed`, in `app/analytics/[liveboardId]/`, and the tile links open it. Nothing needed removing or rerouting.

**What changed:**
- **`LiveboardView.tsx`:** adds the `view-as-table` action with no scoping, and hides TML (`Action.TML`, `ExportTML`, `ImportTML`, `UpdateTML`, `EditTML`). I kept the existing `Action.Explore` hide alongside them. The actions and hidden-actions lists are module constants and the handlers are stable `useCallback`s, so the embed is not rebuilt. `onError` only logs.
- **Data lookup order:** on click the handler tries `embedAnswerData` from the payload first. If that has no rows it tries `answerService.fetchData(0, 101)`, and only with a GUID `vizId` does it call the server route.
- **`TableDialog.tsx`:** a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` as soon as you click, using the brand-* green tokens. It shows a loading state, then the table or a readable error. It has an × button, and Escape and backdrop click close it. Columns sort on header click (click again to reverse, empty values last). Numeric columns are right-aligned, date buckets are shown in UTC, and "First 100 rows" appears when there are more.

ask: Make the embedded analytics match our portal.
finalMessage:
The theme is in place for all three embeds. Typecheck and lint both ran with no errors, and I didn't run any browser tests, as the spec says.

**What changed**
- **`app/components/thoughtspot/theme.ts`** (new) defines the Floyds Bank tokens once. It exports `customizations`, typed with `CustomisationsInterface` and `CustomCssVariables`, and every variable name in it comes from the SDK's `css-variables.d.ts`.
- **`app/components/thoughtspot/init.ts`**: the one shared `init()` now receives `customizations`. Both embeds already render only after `ensureThoughtSpotInit()` resolves, so they wait for that init.
- **`LiveboardView.tsx`** passes `spotterViz` and `spotterChatConfig` as module constants.
- **`SpotterView.tsx`** passes the same `spotterChatConfig`.

**Branding and font**
- Strings are `{ Spotter: "Scout", ThoughtSpot: "Bankalytics" }`.
- `iconSpriteUrl` is a top-level sibling of `style` and `content`. It uses the pinned raw.githubusercontent URL, held in a named constant.
- The only `rules_UNSTABLE` entry is the single `@font-face` for Figtree 400–800. It points at the latin woff2 on fonts.gstatic.com, taken from the Google Fonts CSS.
